audit.process: cursus — agent instructions of a Django monolith, written by hand two years ago
audit.scope: fixtures/repos/django-mvc/repo (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/workflows, guardrail tests, admin, docs/)

elements.finding: File written with care and never reread: three rules are still worth gold (e-mails, capacity, applied migrations), but none has a guardrail, one cites a job that no longer exists, the test command fails, two constraints are contradicted by the repository, and a third of the file is generic content or instructions for another generation of models. No Mode line, no Forbidden, no dates.
elements.target: An AGENTS.md of fewer than 60 lines: delegation mode, table of confirmed commands, the rules with their incident and their real status, a Forbidden section. The e-mail and capacity rules stay word for word in substance.
elements.check: harness status reaches level 1; each "Enforced by" points to a file or a job that exists and that blocks.

elements.finding: Partial copy of AGENTS.md that has diverged: it has the right test command and knows the query test, which AGENTS.md ignores, but its version of the e-mail rule says the opposite of the original ("every enrollment created sends its confirmation") and it repeats the vanished job and Python 3.8. It is the file Claude Code loads.
elements.target: An `@AGENTS.md` stub; what CLAUDE.md knows in addition (test command, catalog/tests/test_queries.py) is carried over into AGENTS.md.
elements.check: CLAUDE.md is one line long; no rule exists in two versions.

elements.finding: A blocking `test` job, healthy for what it carries (makemigrations --check, tests). The `frozen-migrations` job that AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md cite is not in it: nothing rejects the modification of an applied migration.
elements.target: A step that fails when the diff of a PR modifies or deletes an existing file under */migrations/.
elements.check: A PR that touches up enrollments/migrations/0002 is red.

elements.finding: The add form of the admin writes a confirmed Enrollment without going through services.enroll(): the capacity rule is already bypassed in the repository that declares it. The cancel_selected action, for its part, sends one promotion e-mail per cancelled row.
elements.target: has_add_permission set to false, or an add form that calls services.enroll().
elements.check: An admin test: the direct add of a confirmed enrollment in a full session is refused.

elements.finding: Real guardrail: number of queries pinned for each list page, run by the blocking job.
elements.check: A count() per row in a template makes the test job fail.

elements.finding: The rules of seats, waiting list and sending after commit are tested. These tests do not prove the lock, SQLite ignores it: it is a leak of the rule, not a defect of the file.

process_leaks.rule: No e-mail from a post_save signal nor save(); a bulk job never sends one e-mail per row
process_leaks.if_skipped: Thousands of messages and the SMTP account suspended, as on 18 March 2024 (docs/postmortems/2024-03-bulk-confirmations.md). The rule is already violated on a small scale by the admin action cancel_selected, and CLAUDE.md:18 says the reverse.
process_leaks.guard_tool: A test that fails if a receiver is connected to post_save of a model of the project, and one test per bulk job that counts mail.outbox

process_leaks.rule: Every enrollment goes through enrollments.services.enroll(), which locks the session (select_for_update) before counting the seats
process_leaks.if_skipped: More confirmed than seats, as on 9 September 2024. The tests run under SQLite, which ignores the lock; the admin already writes enrollments without going through the service.
process_leaks.guard_tool: A PostgreSQL job with a concurrency test on enroll(), and a check that rejects Enrollment.objects.create and bulk_create outside enrollments/services.py

process_leaks.rule: A migration already applied is never modified
process_leaks.if_skipped: Production keeps the old schema while everything is green here. The file says the rule is enforced by the frozen-migrations job, absent from .github/workflows/ci.yml: guardrail lying by drift.
process_leaks.guard_tool: A step of ci.yml that compares the existing files of */migrations/ with the target branch

guarded_rules.rule: A list page does not run one query per row
A model change is delivered with the file that makemigrations generates

removals.text: Follow PEP 8, lines of 100 characters at most.
Give clear names to variables and functions.
A docstring for every public function.
Think step by step and announce your plan before writing code.
Do not invent Django APIs: if you are not sure a function exists, say so instead of guessing.
Always give the complete file, never an excerpt with `# ... rest unchanged`
The code must run under Python 3.8, the version of the production server
Python 3.8 on the server: no `match`, no `X | Y`.
Stay on the Django 4.2 LTS APIs, the host only validates LTS versions
E-mails: every enrollment created sends its confirmation, through `enrollments/notifications.py`. No signal.

remediation.action: Rewrite AGENTS.md at level 1: mode, confirmed commands, rules with incident and real status, Forbidden; remove the lines listed in removals after the two questions to the owner.
Carry the test command and the query test over into AGENTS.md, then reduce CLAUDE.md to `@AGENTS.md`.
Add the step that rejects the modification of an existing migration.
remediation.check: A PR that touches up an applied migration is red.

remediation.action: Close the direct add of an enrollment in the admin, or route it through services.enroll().
remediation.check: Admin test on a full session.

unverified: The select_for_update lock: no PostgreSQL database available, SQLite ignores it.
The version of Python and Django in production: deduced from requirements.txt and ci.yml, to be confirmed by the owner.
